questions.prompt: The brave soldier chose to die for his country rather than surrender.
questions.answer: Mīles fortis prō patriā morī māluit quam sē dēdere.

questions.prompt: One consul spoke for all the citizens in the assembly.
questions.answer: Ūnus cōnsul prō omnibus cīvibus in contiōne dīxit.

questions.prompt: For the size of the army, the supplies were scarce.
questions.answer: Prō magnitūdine exercitūs commeātūs rārī erant.

questions.prompt: These laws were established for the safety of the people.
questions.answer: Hae lēgēs prō salūte populī cōnstitūtae sunt.

questions.prompt: The general wrote to the senate about the enemy's flight.
questions.answer: Imperātor ad senātum dē fugā hostium scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: Weary from the march, the legions hastened to the river.
questions.answer: Legiōnēs itinere fessae ad flūmen contendērunt.

questions.prompt: The messenger, sent at dawn, ran to the city gates.
questions.answer: Nūntius aurōrā missus ad portās urbis cucurrit.

questions.prompt: The prudent king sent envoys to the neighboring peoples.
questions.answer: Rēx prūdēns lēgātōs ad fīnitimōs populōs mīsit.

questions.prompt: The young warrior mingled with the fierce men in battle.
questions.answer: Iuvenis sē virīs ferōcibus in proeliō miscuit.

questions.prompt: You contend with Homer himself in singing songs.
questions.answer: Homērō ipsī carmina canendō contendis.

questions.prompt: The soldiers clasped hand with hand and swore an oath.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs dextrae dextram iūnxērunt et iūrāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The exile mingled with the crowd and escaped unharmed.
questions.answer: Exsul turbae sē miscuit et incolumis effūgit.

questions.prompt: The loyal friend spoke in behalf of the accused man.
questions.answer: Amīcus fīdus prō reō accūsātō dīxit.

questions.prompt: The captive was punished instead of his lord.
questions.answer: Captīvus prō dominō suō pūnītus est.

questions.prompt: These words were spoken on behalf of the ancient law.
questions.answer: Haec verba prō lēge antīquā dicta sunt.

questions.prompt: In proportion to their wealth, the citizens gave gifts.
questions.answer: Prō dīvitiīs suīs cīvēs dōna dedērunt.

questions.prompt: For his age, the boy showed remarkable wisdom.
questions.answer: Prō aetāte suā puer mīram prūdentiam praebuit.

questions.prompt: The territory was narrow for the great multitude of men.
questions.answer: Prō multitūdine hominum fīnēs angustī erant.

questions.prompt: In proportion to the danger, the reward was small.
questions.answer: Prō perīculō praemium exiguum fuit.

questions.prompt: The wounded captive wrote a letter to his weeping mother.
questions.answer: Captīvus saucius mātrī flentī epistulam scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: At dawn the fleet sailed to the distant island.
questions.answer: Aurōrā classis ad īnsulam remōtam nāvigāvit.

questions.prompt: The river mingles its waters with the vast sea.
questions.answer: Flūmen aquās suās magnō marī miscet.

questions.prompt: The old man, clinging to hope, endured his grief.
questions.answer: Senex speī haerēns maerōrem suum tolerāvit.
